subject.title: Backup: add encrypted snapshot backup flow

question: Should OpenClaw core accept this folder-backed encrypted snapshot/restore config surface, or should core stay with local archive export/verify while off-machine encrypted backup flows live in ClawHub/plugin tooling?
rationale: This PR adds persistent config, destructive restore behavior, encrypted snapshot storage, and cloud-drive-style workflow semantics, so automation cannot choose the permanent core product boundary after code defects are fixed.

options.title: Proceed after hardening
options.body: Require the listed safety fixes, a clean rebase, upgrade/fresh-install tests, and redacted real setup/run/list/restore proof before considering this as a core feature.

options.title: Narrow to archive hardening
options.body: Ask for a smaller PR that only upstreams backup export/verify hardening aligned with current main and defers snapshot workflow design.

options.title: Move snapshot flow outside core
options.body: Keep core focused on local archive semantics and route cloud/off-machine encrypted backup workflows through ClawHub/plugin packages such as the keepmyclaw-style integration mentioned in discussion.

recommendation.title: Proceed after hardening
recommendation.body: Require the listed safety fixes, a clean rebase, upgrade/fresh-install tests, and redacted real setup/run/list/restore proof before considering this as a core feature.

likelyOwner.reason: gumadeiras merged and hardened the original backup CLI surface and is the strongest history-backed owner for deciding whether this extension belongs in core.
